criteria.note: draft_plan_from_requirements (.warp/tracker_intake.py) turns a structured requirements page into a warp.plan/v1 DRAFT: intake_plan_from_requirements reads the page THROUGH the shipped WARP-0603 seam (adapter.read_item, the FakeTracker in the gate and a ConfluenceCloudAdapter in production), it reuses the WARP-0607 parse_requirements to extract the page's Outcomes AND the Deliverables work breakdown (no second parser), resolves the target repo with the REUSED WARP-0601 resolver (resolve_repo, a warp-repo:<repo> page label), and renders a plan whose OUTCOMES come from the page's Outcomes with ONE work item per named Deliverable, bound to the resolved repo, the source page linked in intake_source. It FAILS CLOSED by name (IntakeError) when the routing signal is missing/unknown/ambiguous, exactly like the spec intake (the except on TrackerRoutingError re-raises IntakeError; no default repo). Confirmed by reading the source and by the selftest WARP-1007 block: a resolvable page drafts bound to repo-a, outcomes equal the two page Outcome bullets, the three work items equal the three Deliverable bullets, the source page (PLP-1, confluence) is linked in source and intake_source, and intake_plan_from_requirements drafts the same through the FakeTracker seam.

The rendered plan is a VALID warp.plan/v1 and is a DRAFT that the machine never approves. render_plan_markdown feeds V.check_plan which returns 0 in the selftest, and I independently rendered and validated it (check_plan==0 over a temp dir with no wired tracker config). It is status: draft with NO approved_by and NO approved_at; check_plan (.warp/validate.py line 474-477) enforces that a plan leaves draft ONLY with approved_by AND approved_at, so status:draft plus their absence makes a human the sole path out of draft (PLAN-0010 NG1). The selftest asserts status draft and approved_by absent. It is a deterministic non-LLM structural transform reusing parse_requirements and resolve_repo, adding no second parser and no agent/LLM/network call (grep of the W7 functions finds only a comment mentioning 'no agent call'). Page content is untrusted: every front-matter value is sanitized by the SAME _fm_safe guard (collapses all control chars below space), so a malicious page title with embedded newlines cannot open a new front-matter key. I independently rendered an evil page whose title attempts id:/schema:/status:ready/approved_by/approved_at injection: the injected keys are absent from the markdown, the plan keeps the generator's PLAN-9004 id, stays a draft with no approved_by, and still passes check_plan. The generator fails SAFE to one outcome and one work item so the rendered plan is always valid.

The generator supplies ONLY the generation step and wires NO new tracker writes. draft_plan_from_requirements / intake_plan_from_requirements / render_plan_markdown are pure (no network, no file write, no adapter write path); intake_plan_from_requirements's only adapter touch is read_item (a read). The live epic-plus-child projection that consumes an approved plan is WARP-1006 (already shipped), unchanged here: the reviewed diff touches no mirror, runner, bridge, promote gate, reassign/links, or epic/child creation. The end-to-end chain (kickoff ticket -> plan draft -> human approval -> WARP-1006 epic mirror -> children) is complete with this generation step in place.

findings.text: Non-blocking, by design. The generator emits PLACEHOLDER work-item spec ids (WARP-%04d, always the WARP- prefix regardless of the resolved repo's real spec-id prefix) and a placeholder plan_id default of PLAN-0000, because it cannot know the target repo's prefix or the next free plan id. The docstring, the capability note, and the drafted plan's Intent all say a human allocates a real spec id per work item and a real plan id on approval before any work is built. check_plan accepts the placeholders (spec id matches PREFIX-0000; PLAN-0000 matches PLAN-\d+), so the draft is valid and the allocation is a deliberate human refinement step, not a defect.
